time_budget.pattern_detail: Up to ~8 hours in a single wake-period, but not consecutively. Long sessions with breaks, not marathon runs. Within a session, harder tasks first, finish each completely before moving on (no half-done tasks).
time_budget.wake_window_detail: Husband works 6pm-6am on certain nights; user keeps schedule synced to his. Wake window is roughly evening (6pm onward) through morning. Sleep during the day.
time_budget.daylight_coordination_purpose: Same-day sponsor/brand email reply, real-time coordination with US-business-hours partners. Not a regular work block — a focused coordination window.
time_budget.daylight_coordination_pattern: Anchor to husband's lunch break or a fixed time. Batch-process sponsor email, brand outreach, calls, and any other time-sensitive coordination in this window. ~30 min/day, 4-6 days/week, or longer block 2x/week.
time_budget.schedule_decision_rationale: Relationship-sync preference (keep schedule aligned with husband) is the primary constraint. User confirmed willingness to add focused daylight hours for career coordination. Bolt's role: shift cron jobs to evening wake-hours, use Apple Reminders as async inbox, surface daylight-coordination items so user can batch-process them in 2-3 focused hours/week.
time_budget.schedule_mode_note: Mostly night (≈37 hrs/week evening-through-morning) + small daylight coordination window (2-3 hrs/week). Daylight is for time-sensitive coordination only, not regular creator work.
time_budget.allocation_note: Working default from the 40-hour week the user already described. Brand/sponsor hours include the 2–3h daylight coordination window. Numbers can move later; this unblocks planning.

hard_constraints.text: No content that sells a hyped product as if it works. If Billy already has something that's hyped but doesn't deliver, cover it as an honest review — and pair it with a similar product that actually works. Never skip the dud just because it's trendy, and never recommend the dud.
hard_constraints.rationale: Authenticity includes reviewing the hype you actually own. The moat is the honest verdict plus a working alternative, not silence and not fake praise.

hard_constraints.text: Bolt prioritizes direction-finding over execution. When given a to-do list, push back with 'do we know this is the right list?' before charging ahead.
hard_constraints.rationale: User's bottleneck is no roadmap. Following a list without validating direction wastes the user's bursty time budget on the wrong things.

hard_constraints.text: Bolt captures the process of building this career, not just the outputs. The goal is producing a roadmap another person could follow end-to-end.
hard_constraints.rationale: User explicitly asked for this. The roadmap must be operable by a stranger, not just notes for the user.

hard_constraints.text: Work pattern is bursty night-shift with focused daylight coordination: wake window roughly evening-through-morning (synced with husband's 6pm-6am work schedule). Within a wake-period, max ~8 hours, not consecutive. Within a session, work on harder tasks first and finish each one completely before starting the next. No half-done tasks left open when a session ends. Plus 2-3 hours/week of focused daylight coordination for time-sensitive sponsor/brand reply — anchored to a fixed time (e.g. husband's lunch break), not scattered.
hard_constraints.rationale: User stated this explicitly during Q3 (bursty pattern), confirmed during follow-up (harder-first, complete-before-moving-on, scoped to within-session), chose to keep night schedule on 2026-07-29 for relationship-sync reasons, then on 2026-07-29 added willingness to include 2-3 focused daylight hours/week for coordination. This is compatible with parallel-trial lane mix across the week and with durable-content production model.

hard_constraints.text: Bolt does not recommend content lanes, topics, or products unless they've been cross-checked against the user's actual interests and history. 'Would you want to be known for this?' is a hard gate, not a soft preference.
hard_constraints.rationale: Q4 user words: 'I have ideas but nothing truly authentic or passionate enough to honestly make worthy content of. It doesn't feel authentic to me.'

hard_constraints.text: Authenticity outranks profitability. A deal, lane, or product that pays well but doesn't pass the 'believe in / stand behind / trust it' test is rejected, regardless of upside.
hard_constraints.rationale: Q4 user quote: 'I don't want to be known for something I don't really care about. Even if it makes me rich. It sounds great, but I want to believe in it, stand behind it, and trust it.' This is THE foundational test for every recommendation.

hard_constraints.text: No content, partnerships, sponsorships, or product coverage that supports Donald Trump, MAGA, or anything that insults the user's intelligence. Including indirect associations (e.g., a brand whose parent company is Trump-affiliated, products whose marketing aligns with that brand).
hard_constraints.rationale: Q7 user words: 'I will not support Donald Trump or MAGA supported items or anything that insults intelligence.'

revenue_scenario.framing: Don't budget against a specific dollar amount. Budget against life-changes — what shifts in your day-to-day at each tier? Pick the number that triggers the change you actually want.

tier_1_0_to_500.what_it_looks_like: First sponsor deals, learning what to charge, building relationships. Twitch audience conversion starts here.
tier_1_0_to_500.life_change: User: even $1k/mo means breathing fuller and smiling more. Proof this is not a made-up failure. Attitude and motivation shift first; the calendar may not.

tier_2_500_to_3000.duration: 6-18 months typical for honest-product creators who actually do the work
tier_2_500_to_3000.what_it_looks_like: Consistent sponsor deals, Amazon affiliate starts compounding, some product seeding (free products = cost-of-living offset).
tier_2_500_to_3000.life_change: User: $3k/mo is confidence that this is an actual career they built and wouldn't be embarrassed behind. $1k already changes the feeling; $3k names it as the job.

tier_3_3000_to_8000.what_it_looks_like: Multiple sponsor relationships, regular event invitations, possible Patreon/membership. Dream Con / Marvel-tier recognition lives here or above.
tier_3_3000_to_8000.life_change: Creator becomes the actual job. Day-to-day fully shifts.

tier_4_above_8000.what_it_looks_like: Brand ambassador deals, retainers, event appearance fees, scaled affiliate.
tier_4_above_8000.life_change: Top-tier. Comfortable full-time income from the work.

levers_that_move_revenue_up: Travel content commands premium per-deal rates (companies pay more for creator-on-site filming than 60-second reviews)
Honest-takes command a premium (trust is the actual product)
Event hosting is a separate revenue line (often on top of content deal)
Multi-platform amplification (TikTok + YouTube + X + blog doubles value without doubling work)
levers_that_move_revenue_down: Audience size vs engagement: trust beats vanity numbers, but there's still a floor
Inconsistency: 25/25/25/25 lane mix means each lane needs to produce enough to count
Authenticity tax: saying no to a deal is a real cost; pays back in long-term brand relationships
C7 filter closes some doors; other doors open with brands that specifically want honest creators
what_bolt_cant_predict: Which brands will pay at your tier
Whether gaming/tech or skincare monetizes faster than general product reviews
Whether 'creating with Marvel' is realistic at all

user_target.what_changes: Attitude, motivation, and confidence — not a different lifestyle calendar. $1k/mo is enough to start breathing fuller and smiling more. $3k/mo is being able to say this is an actual career they built and wouldn't be embarrassed behind.
user_target.user_words: Would probably be my attitude, motivation and confidence in saying this is an actual career that I built and wouldn't be embarrassed behind. I haven't been not doing anything, I just don't have any wind behind me or a push to keep myself motivated because I'm making everything up so I've had the expectation of failing. Even at $1k a month, I'd start breathing fuller and smiling more.
user_target.implication_for_bolt: Do not treat the work as 'nothing happening until $3k.' The motivation gap is missing proof and a real roadmap, not missing effort. Celebrate and track the path to $1k/mo as the first emotional win. Never frame the current work as expected failure.
